# FROZEN expected text for fixture A (the public demo course). Lines: W|week|rule or outline|text  - the printed text, exact.
# Q lines: Q|week|pinpoint|source file|quoted words. Each quote must occur, ignoring case and spacing, INSIDE the cited paragraph of the source file ("para N");
# Van Gend and Costa have no paragraph numbers in the English text, so they are cited by ECLI (the quote is checked in the whole file). Written by hand from the Cellar texts, not from pack output.
# Changed only with a logged reason in flows/printpack/HISTORY.md.
W|1|rule|**In one glance** Dassonville (Case 8/74, para 5): "all trading rules enacted by Member States which are capable of hindering, directly or indirectly, actually or potentially, intra-Community trade are to be considered as measures having an effect equivalent to quantitative restrictions". Keck (Joined Cases C-267/91 and C-268/91, para 16): "contrary to what has previously been decided" certain selling arrangements fall outside that formula "so long as those provisions apply to all relevant traders operating within the national territory and so long as they affect in the same manner, in law and in fact, the marketing of domestic products and of those from other Member States".
W|1|outline|The Dassonville formula
W|1|outline|Mutual recognition and mandatory requirements
W|1|outline|Selling arrangements
W|1|outline|Market access
W|2|rule|**In one glance** Van Gend en Loos (Case 26/62, ECLI:EU:C:1963:1): "a new legal order of international law". Costa v ENEL (Case 6/64, ECLI:EU:C:1964:66): the Treaty's own legal system "became an integral part of the legal systems of the Member States". Marshall (Case 152/84, para 48): "a directive may not of itself impose obligations on an individual".
W|2|outline|Direct effect
W|2|outline|Primacy
W|2|outline|The national court sets aside conflicting law
W|2|outline|Directives and individuals
